items.q: Opioid overdose triad requiring naloxone is what?
items.exp: Pinpoint pupils, hypoventilation and coma define opioid toxicity; naloxone titrated to adequate breathing (not necessarily full alertness) reverses it. Withdrawal shows opposite dilated, hyperactive gut picture.
r: Incorrect. That is withdrawal physiology.
Correct. Miosis, slow breathing, coma.
Incorrect. Rigidity fever suggests serotonin or neuroleptic syndromes.
Incorrect. Those are alcohol withdrawal events.
items.kp: Small pupils, slow breaths, out cold: naloxone.

items.q: Why observe after successful naloxone reversal of methadone overdose?
o: Naloxone half life is shorter than methadone, causing re sedation
items.exp: Naloxone lasts roughly 30 to 90 minutes while methadone and modified release opioids persist many hours, so recurrence of respiratory depression needs observation and sometimes infusion.
r: Incorrect. Seizures are not naloxone routine effect.
Correct. Short antidote versus long poison.
Incorrect. No such conversion explains it.
Incorrect. Tolerance dynamics differ.
items.kp: Antidote fades first: watch them breathe again.

items.q: Buprenorphine induction should start when patient shows what state and why?
o: Mild to moderate withdrawal (COWS threshold); avoids precipitated withdrawal
items.exp: High affinity partial agonist displaces full agonists; giving it while receptors are occupied plunges patients into precipitated withdrawal. Waiting for objective withdrawal signs (COWS guided) makes induction tolerable.
r: Incorrect. Intoxication occupancy maximises precipitation.
Correct. Wait for mild withdrawal signs.
Incorrect. Methadone occupancy is worst timing.
Incorrect. Office induction is standard.

items.q: Methadone maintenance signature cardiac risk needing ECG vigilance is what?
items.exp: Methadone prolongs QT dose dependently (risk rises over 100 mg range and with interacting CYP drugs or hypokalaemia), so ECG at induction and dose changes follows local protocol.
r: Correct. QT prolongation with torsades risk.
Incorrect. Bradycardia alone is not signature.
Incorrect. Block is not universal effect.
Incorrect. Pericarditis unrelated.

items.q: Opioid withdrawal in healthy adults is best characterised how versus alcohol withdrawal?
o: Extremely distressing but rarely medically dangerous; alcohol withdrawal can kill
items.exp: Opioid withdrawal lacks seizures and delirium tremens equivalents; danger concentrates in dehydration vulnerability (pregnancy, comorbidity, neonates). Alcohol and benzodiazepine withdrawal are the lethal ones.
r: Incorrect. Seizures belong to GABA drug withdrawal.
Correct. Miserable but rarely lethal; alcohol withdrawal kills.
Incorrect. Withdrawal is intensely unpleasant.
Incorrect. Consciousness stays clear.
items.kp: Opioid withdrawal tortures; alcohol withdrawal kills.

items.q: After detoxification without maintenance, the major cause of fatal relapse overdose is what?
o: Lost tolerance meeting previously tolerated dose
items.exp: Abstinence resets tolerance within weeks, so returning to old doses overwhelms respiration; this post detox and post prison window is among deadliest, motivating maintenance and naloxone provision.
r: Incorrect. Tolerance falls, not rises.
Correct. Lost tolerance plus old dose kills.
Incorrect. Liver not central mechanism.
Incorrect. Naloxone still works if given.
items.kp: Clean weeks erase tolerance, old dose becomes lethal.

items.q: Naltrexone maintenance for opioid disorder requires what before starting?
o: Opioid free interval (about 7 to 10 days) to avoid precipitated withdrawal
items.exp: Antagonist in occupied receptors precipitates severe withdrawal, so confirmed abstinence interval and negative challenge approaches precede oral or depot naltrexone in motivated patients.
r: Incorrect. Active use precipitates withdrawal.
Correct. Week opioid free first.
Incorrect. Sedatives do not enable induction.
Incorrect. Pregnancy favours agonist maintenance.
items.kp: Antagonist last, after receptors empty a week.

items.q: In pregnancy with opioid use disorder, recommended pharmacotherapy is what?
items.exp: Maintenance stabilises maternal levels, reduces relapse and illicit use, improving fetal outcomes despite neonatal withdrawal syndrome, which is treatable; detox relapse cycles harm more. Buprenorphine (often without naloxone combination per local practice) is alternative.
r: Incorrect. Forced detox relapses dangerously.
Correct. Agonist maintenance in pregnancy.
Incorrect. Antagonist data limited, not first line.
Incorrect. Untreated disorder harms mother and fetus.
items.kp: Maintain the mother, treat the newborn.

items.q: Co prescribing which drug class most multiplies opioid overdose death?
items.exp: Sedative co depressants synergise respiratory depression; opioid benzodiazepine combinations carry boxed warnings, requiring taper of one or both, naloxone supply and documented rationale when unavoidable.
r: Incorrect. SSRIs interact modestly (tramadol serotonin caution).
Correct. Benzodiazepines multiply overdose.
Incorrect. Antihistamines sedate mildly less central.
Incorrect. Statins irrelevant.
items.kp: Opioid plus benzo is the lethal stack.

items.q: Harm reduction services with proven mortality and infection benefit include what?
o: Needle exchange, naloxone distribution, substitution therapy and HIV hepatitis testing
items.exp: Sterile equipment, take home naloxone, maintenance therapy and blood borne virus care reduce deaths and transmission without increasing use, forming evidence based public health core.
r: Correct. Proven harm reduction bundle.
Incorrect. Lectures alone lack outcome evidence.
Incorrect. Punitive testing deters care.
Incorrect. Vaccination protects, withholding harms.
items.kp: Keep people alive and uninfected until recovery.
